problems.problem: Contact detail crop [434,1099,1035,1349] shows the bottle base ending at y=1239 with only a hairline dark rim: the cleft-slate texture below the base keeps the same brightness and grain as the surrounding plane, with no occlusion gradient, no cast shadow lobe and no reflected light kick at the glass edge, so the executed contact shadow (opacity 0.55, blur 18, offset_y 0) is not reading. Worse, the base sits ~110px BELOW the rough cleft front edge of the ledge (edge at y≈1090-1130 in the poster), i.e. on the darker vertical front face of the ledge rather than on its lit top plane, so the bottle reads as pasted onto a cliff face. Geometry confirms base 1239 vs ledge top plane ≈1000-1090.

The ledge band runs behind the bottle at y≈1000-1130 while the bottle base lands at 1239, so the support plane and the product disagree; the diagonal soft sweep from upper left models only the wall and never touches the bottle's left shoulder or cap, leaving product light (bright studio frontal) disconnected from background light. No studio equipment is visible, but the illumination logic still mismatches the unmodified bright product photograph.

The previous georgia.ttf upgrade was REJECTED by the renderer (execution_feedback Critic-safe-groups), so the left inscription column still renders in default msyh.ttc sans: title bbox height only ~35px (size 46) with loose untracked lines for logo/title/subtitle. Against the references' confident logotype handling (Chanel's heavy tracked band, Diptyque's integrated display serif) the type block stays generic and under-scaled for the luxury concept; the earlier patch also tried to change three fields at once, which failed validation.

The carved-baseline rule sits at y=612 while the subtitle block ends at y=544, leaving a ~68px dead gap that disconnects the rule from the type block; combined with the empty uniform slate in the lower-left two-thirds, the left-inscription/right-image grid loses its bottom anchor once the eye discovers the bottle is not standing on the visible ledge.
